newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London pared some losses after bargain-hunting to end above new four-week lows of $1,520 a tonne hit earlier on trade and fund selling. Reports that Brazilian coffee stored in Trieste, Italy, for 10 years awaiting the outcome of a court decision has gone bad and that its release to the market will have no effect on prices, aided sentiment. The coffee, which is more than 15 years old and was poorly stored, is expected to be used in very small quantities, no more than 10 percent of the total blend in the soluble industry, it was said. In July 1996, the European court ruled Brazil must compensate companies for losses in the so-called Patricia operation in 1986. The operation was masterminded by the Brazilian government to hike coffee prices.

In New York, arabica futures rebounded to end higher, and trade and speculative buying erased early losses and touched off buy-stops above 112 cents/lb in the December contract. Ideas the market was overdone to the downside and in need of a correction, as well as talk that the Brazilian 1996/97 crop will be smaller than expected, and the political problems in Colombia, which could affect coffee exports, aided sentiment.

BRAZIL - A recent estimate of the Espirito Santo coffee crop has prompted the Brazilian government to settle on a national 1996/97 (May/April) crop estimate of between 24 and 25 million 60-kg bags, Commerce Ministry commodities secretary, Mauricio Assis said. He added the national estimate had been drawn up following the completion of a survey of the Espirito Santo crop by the Emater agricultural studies group. The group put the state's 1996/97 crop at 4.97 million bags. Assis cited a similar study coordinated by the Minas Gerais state agricultural federation putting the state's 1996/97 crop at 12.4 million bags. He added the crop in Sao Paulo is estimated at between 3.4 and 3.5 million bags, the Parana crop at between 1.1 and 1.2 million bags and other states' production totalling 2.3 million bags. Assis said the Industry and Commerce Ministry will shortly begin discussions towards consolidating the regional estimates to once again produce official government estimates in future years.

COLOMBIA - It is feared that increased rebel activity could threaten Colombia's coffee exports. A western diplomat, citing military intelligence reports, said recently that Colombia's rebels were about 10,000-strong in 1994 and were expected to double their armies by mid-1998. The Colombian army, meanwhile, is about 120,000-strong and its commander, General Harold Bedoya, said in a recent interview that he needed three times as many men to counter the growing threat posed by rebels. Diplomates said the security situation is going from bad to worse. Press reports said that president Ernesto Samper has essentially done nothing while Colombia burned around him. It was added that the country is disintegrating in the shaky and inept hands of the country's leaders.

E.D. & F. MAN - According to London trade house E.D. & F. Man, consumer stocks of green coffee dropped to 8.7 million 60-kg bags in July 1996, down from 8.8 million bags in June and 11.4 million bags in July 1995. However, Man said that consumer stocks have shown no clear trend during the last four months. It was added that GCA stocks have fallen, but that this has been compensated by a rise in European and Japanese stocks. European stocks were swollen by the front-loading of Central American shipments in the second quarter of the year, although the bulk of this stock is already committed to roasters, Man said. It was added that warehouses report that arrivals had been low in August but so has roaster offtake as roasting plants closed down for the holiday period. It was added that warehouses are expecting business to increase moving into September with further arrivals of new crop Brazils.

ROMANIA - Romania imported 192,100 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, nearly 70 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 39 percent to 243,200 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Brazil (37,600 vs 51,600 bags) and Indonesia (89,900 vs 3,900 bags).
